classification.difficultyReason: Select inverse tangent from the two labelled legs, then use the supplied 180° plus angle expression and round the bearing to minutes.

content.prompt: A pigeon was released from $A$ and flew 5.3 km due south before it turned west and continued to fly for another 17 km to reach $B$. Calculate the true bearing $(180^\circ+\theta)$ of the pigeon at $B$ from $A$. Answer to the nearest minute.

spec.description: A is above the right-angle vertex; B is west of it. The compass is centred at A and theta lies between the southward leg and AB. Decorative blue geometry becomes black.
spec.mathematics: AC = 5.3 km due south; CB = 17 km due west. The angle at A has opposite side CB and adjacent side AC.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and theta are shown; calculated angles and the bearing are withheld.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\tan\theta &= \frac{17}{5.3}\\\theta &= \tan^{-1}\!\left(\frac{17}{5.3}\right)\end{align*}$$
$B$ is southwest of $A$, so the true bearing is:
$$\begin{align*}\text{Bearing} &= 180^\circ+\tan^{-1}\!\left(\frac{17}{5.3}\right)\\&\approx 252^\circ41'\end{align*}$$
